- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- Model consistently overpredicts prices in early forecast windows (e.g., first 5–7 days) after a spike; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged rally; cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high to prevent overcorrection.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive (≥ 0.0) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize reversal; add a 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature sell-off.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early days of the 30-day window; apply a 1–2% downward correction for days 1–5 to align with observed lagged behavior.
